smimon wrote: Haha, no worries.

Go Tools --> Options and set the number of bars in history/chart to something 1,000,000 - the option isn't in the dropdown, but you can overtype it. You need to close and relaunch MT4 for this setting to get picked up correctly. i.imgur.com/c652DOJ.png

Next, press F2 to go to history centre, find the symbol you want on the left, and click download. This might take a while. Everything going well, all the history should then appear. However, the history handling in MT4 isn't the best. You might have to click download again, and get it to "recalculate all timeframes", or right click on the chart and hit "Refresh" if strange gaps appear in the data. Also a relaunch doesn't hurt. i.imgur.com/YZ8uvwe.png

Eventually, it settles down and should be ok.

A warning though - if you've got a number of charts open, having this many history bars can use a lot of memory, and MT4 can start bugging or crashing out. Gaps can randomly appear in the data, or it gets stuck on "Waiting for update" when you switch TF. A relaunch usually fixes this.

In the worst case, it will crash completely, with the "Metatrader has stopped working" windows dialog, Every time you relaunch, after 30 seconds it happens again. To clear this, you have to open, quickly close down all charts, close, relaunch with no charts open, and then it's fine.

1,000,000 seems to be about the sweet spot, I only get very occasional crashes with this. Any more, and it becomes almost unusable. I actually have a separate instance of MT4 with 5,000,000 bars so I can look back on M1 about a decade, which I just fire up when I need it, and then close down again.

Have fun;-)

blackmovie wrote: hi smimon, great trade. Some question on the chart below.

I've seen the question "how do you know if a FL is important or not" a few times, so as best as I can explain it:

- it is important is there is a big surge from it - it is important if it holds price up/down several times - this is perhaps the key indicator - it is important if it is the last s urge into a top/bottom, that is a FTR from taking out an opposing important FL

When you bear these 3 things in mind, the level on Gold was important because:

In terms of "knowing" it will hold, you don't - at least I don't with that much confidence! However what I do know is we are guaranteed to get a decent bounce from it - there are simply too many orders in levels like that for it not to give a good bounce. It's a scalp-and-see PO really when you try and pick a top like that. If you've analysed the level correctly, it's a great potential runner. If you've analysed it wrong, you're usually stopped out in 10 seconds;-)

Some thoughts on important news announcements that effect fundamental valuations of currencies, and the levels that these create becoming important in the future.

Here's some recent action on GU, around an area I've previously analysed - what is the significance of this level that keeps rejecting price? Conventional FTR analysis suggests it should be of little importance in the scheme of things. (excuse the mess of other levels on the chart, they tend to accumulate over time and I have to spring clean occasionally)

When we consider however the SNB announcement, and the shift in fundamental valuations of currencies that occurred at that point, the significance of the level becomes more apparent.

Now bear in mind, I'm backwards rationalising this - I've been caught out by this level already, not expecting it to have the significance it did. But after seeing how important it has become, it's made me go away and try to think why. At present, this is the best answer I can come up with.

Here's another example on EU, recently. The Fed interest rate decision at 1900 on the 28th Jan put a ceiling on the valuation of EU, which has formed a barrier to price several times already. If this level breaks, it could well be significant in the scheme of things.

In general, moving forwards, I'm going to pay more attention to these important fundamental levels, and the FTRs created when they are taken out.

Hi Smimon,

your journal is great, here is my view on GU

0700 - 1000 is a great time to trade. Things are usually moving into position off the back of the Asian session, and begin forming setups at good levels around 0730. It pays to be in your position by 0730 I've found, since then you're ready for the burst of liquidity 0800-0900 from the London open. Many days there is also some important GBP news at 0930, for more opportunities.

EU long, formed a decent setup, attempted to read price as it was developing. This is something I want to focus on more - it's great to read HTF, and wait only for the best opportunities, but it's quite possible to get a read on what price is doing in between these levels - by watching how bars are forming, how flags are forming and being broken, and which FLs are being respected - and there are many good opportunities to be had.
